title: CyberWolf Web Security Check
description: Questions about browser/server boundaries, access control and secure application design.

questions.prompt: Why is client-side validation not sufficient as the only security control?

options.text: A user can bypass or modify client-side checks

questions.explanation: Client-side checks improve usability, but a client is not trusted. The server must validate data and enforce business rules.

questions.prompt: Where should an application enforce authorization for a sensitive record?

options.text: Only by hiding the menu item in the browser
On the server for each protected action or object

questions.explanation: Server-side authorization must validate that the authenticated identity has permission for the specific action and object. UI restrictions are not security boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which practice most directly helps prevent SQL injection in database queries?

options.text: Concatenate user input into SQL strings
Hide database errors only in the browser

questions.explanation: Parameterized queries keep data separate from SQL command structure, reducing the risk that untrusted input is interpreted as executable query syntax.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of context-aware output encoding?

options.text: To make every browser request anonymous
To ensure untrusted data is treated as data in the output context
To disable all JavaScript on the internet

questions.explanation: Correct encoding for the HTML, attribute, URL or JavaScript context helps prevent untrusted data from being interpreted as executable markup or code.

questions.prompt: Which cookie attribute helps prevent JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly instructs browsers to restrict access to the cookie through non-HTTP APIs such as document.cookie. It does not replace other session protections.
